answer: Entropy-gated admission slots: each round, a verifiable random function seeds which identity hashes become eligible, so an attacker cannot precompute which clones will admit. Applicants must then prove a fresh kernel of work tied to their seed before claiming a slot, and slots unused within the round are voided. To fill a garden of N identities, the attacker must run N independent unpredictable work puzzles; since seeds are unknowable in advance, bulk-registered clones mostly land on dead slots, and the shale of wasted compute grows with every clone attempted.
